name: Halton

licensing.selective: No selective licensing scheme in force yet. A scheme was consulted on from 3 August to 18 October 2026 for Central and West Bank, Appleton, Mersey and Weston and Bridgewater wards and part of Highfield (about 43% of the borough's private rented homes); the council had not decided at the time of checking.
licensing.additional: No additional HMO licensing scheme is listed: larger HMOs (five or more people from two or more households) need a national mandatory licence.

housing: Halton is made up of the two towns of Widnes and Runcorn on either side of the Mersey, linked by the Silver Jubilee and Mersey Gateway bridges. The older streets near both town centres and at West Bank are Victorian terraces, which hold much of the private rented stock, while Runcorn has large new town estates of the 1960s and 1970s with footpath layouts and many terraced homes. Private renting is lower than across the North West but grew quickly between 2011 and 2021.
checkinTips: Victorian terraces in Widnes and Runcorn Old Town: check for damp at the base of walls and in rear kitchens, and photograph yards and back entries.
New town houses in Palacefields, Windmill Hill and Castlefields: record flat roofs, garages or car ports, communal footpaths and fencing.
Homes near the Mersey at West Bank and Hale: look for signs of damp or past flooding in ground-floor rooms.
Flats above shops in the town centres: photograph the separate entrance, stairs, fire alarm and meter cupboards.
Newer homes at Sandymoor: note snagging still outstanding, meter readings and parking allocations.
tenantHelp: Tenants with disrepair, damp or safety problems in a private let can contact Halton Borough Council's housing standards team (environmental health), after first reporting the problem to their landlord.
